blocks.title: Nothing at runtime
blocks.body: Pages are built from files on disk. The CMS is never in the request path, so it can never be the reason a page is slow, or down, or wrong.
blocks.proof: Zero script tags in the built output

blocks.title: Hybrid by default
blocks.body: A region is any slice of a page you opt in — one hero, or the whole site. Everything else stays hand-written code the studio never sees.
blocks.proof: A missing content file renders schema defaults

blocks.title: Not a framework plugin
blocks.body: The integration surface is a schema file and some JSON. Astro, Hugo, Eleventy, Next, Jekyll, and Laravel consume it identically.
blocks.proof: A 120-line Python reader passes the same suite

blocks.title: One commit, or none
blocks.body: An image and the content referencing it land together through the Git Data API. Half-applied content is how a main branch stops building.
blocks.proof: Blob, tree, commit, ref — never one commit per file
